title: Multiway partitioning
text: Compare k parts and refine them by swaps
transcript: Compare round robin, recursive bisection and capacity-legal swaps; calibrate against a tiny exact oracle.

title: Learning goals
text: Compute k-way edge cut · Implement a deterministic round-robin baseline · Compare recursive construction and swap refinement
transcript:
Compute k-way edge cut
Implement a deterministic round-robin baseline
Compare recursive construction and swap refinement
Check area-capacity feasibility
Explain local versus exact optima
Design a fair same-input comparison

title: 01 · The k-way objective
text: Assign every vertex to one of k disjoint, nonempty parts.
transcript: Assign every vertex to one of k disjoint, nonempty parts. In an ordinary graph, an edge contributes its weight once whenever endpoint labels differ. Increasing k does not multiply that charge. Meaningful comparison requires the same input, objective and capacity.

title: 02 · A round-robin baseline
text: Assign input vertex i to i mod k.
transcript: Assign input vertex i to i mod k. At k=3, G01 becomes AD | BE | C. Every edge crosses, so cut=18. Counts 2/2/1 are even, but the method ignores weights. Balanced counts and good connections are separate properties.

title: 03 · Recursive construction
text: Recursive splitting gives DE | ABC, then AB | C, yielding AB | C | DE with cut 8.
transcript: Recursive splitting gives DE | ABC, then AB | C, yielding AB | C | DE with cut 8. It preserves the heavy AB and DE edges. Counts are 2/1/2, so unit areas satisfy capacity 2.

title: 04 · Cross-part swap refinement
transcript: Enumerate pairs in different parts. Hypothetically exchange their labels, check every area against capacity, then compute gain=cut_before−cut_after. Accept the largest strictly positive legal gain, breaking ties by vertex names. Repeat until none exists or the step limit is reached.

title: 05 · Calibrate with an exact tiny solver
text: The oracle enumerates legal nonempty assignments while removing duplicate part-label permutations.
transcript: The oracle enumerates legal nonempty assignments while removing duplicate part-label permutations. For G01, k=3 and capacity 2, its optimum is 8. Agreement proves optimality only for that instance.

title: 06 · Change a weight and rerun
text: Change AB from 5 to 1 at k=3.
transcript: Change AB from 5 to 1 at k=3. Round robin still cuts every edge, reducing its cost from 18 to 14. The spectral and recursive methods solve again and can produce A | BC | DE with cut 5. Inspect actual events; ties or repeated eigenvalues may permit equivalent groupings.

title: 07 · Report a reproducible comparison
text: Record the graph, vertex order, sizes, k, capacity, construction strategy, ties, stop reason, final cut and part areas.
transcript: Record the graph, vertex order, sizes, k, capacity, construction strategy, ties, stop reason, final cut and part areas. Do not rank infeasible rows alongside feasible ones by cost. Report an optimality gap only when an exact result is available.

title: Decision contract
text: Compare round robin, recursive bisection and capacity-legal swaps; calibrate against a tiny exact oracle.
transcript: No improving legal swap or limit

title: Check the common mistakes
transcript: Round robin has counts 2/2/1 but cut 18; recursive gets 8.

title: Test your understanding
text: Predict → run the lab → solve challenges → write two Python functions
transcript: Explain your reasoning with actual output, the objective, constraints and stop reason.
